ActId.description:
An act, scoped to the corpus that knows how to fetch it.

Identity is `(corpus, key)` only. `display_name` is a label that rides along for output, so
the same act named by two callers, one of which knows its title and one of which does not,
is the same act in equality, in hashing and in every set and dict key downstream.

display_name.description: Human title, for output only; never parsed, never identity.
display_name.title: Display Name

ActId.title: ActId

ApplicabilityUnchanged.description: The change does not move the date this provision applies from.
ApplicabilityUnchanged.title: ApplicabilityUnchanged

ApplicabilityUnknown.description:
The applicability date could not be read deterministically, which is the honest answer.

Attaching a date to a provision set is prose, with exceptions and conditions. Many
unknowns is the correct outcome; the model never fills one in.
ApplicabilityUnknown.title: ApplicabilityUnknown

Change.description:
One provision that changed between two versions of one act.

The unit is the top-level provision; `changed_within` carries the finer coordinates
the diff could localise, and `dates_removed`/`dates_added` the machine-readable dates that
moved. Both are detail attached to the unit, never a second unit of their own.

`amending_acts` is attribution, not classification: it says which acts a signal names as
amending this unit. The structural diff carries no such fact, so the field is filled by
corroboration and is empty when no signal names one.

amending_acts.description: Acts a signal names as amending this unit; empty when none names one.
amending_acts.title: Amending Acts

changed_within.description: Sub-provision coordinates whose own text differs: detail, not the unit.
changed_within.title: Changed Within

dates_added.description: Machine-readable dates the provision carries after and not before.
dates_added.title: Dates Added

dates_removed.description: Machine-readable dates the provision carried before and not after.
dates_removed.title: Dates Removed

dispute_reason.description: Which signal disagreed and how; None exactly when not disputed. Derived from `signals`, never stored apart from them.

disputed.description: Signals disagree. Derived from `signals`, not free.
disputed.title: Disputed

previous_location.description: The location a renumbered provision had before.

table_entries.description: The keyed diff of the unit's table entries. None means not read: no profiled table in the unit on either side, or a document written before schema 1.3. An empty delta means read, and no keyed entry changed.

Change.title: Change

ChangeType.description:
How a provision changed. Assigned by the diff and its classification, never by a model.

`RENUMBERED` and `DEFERRED` are carried from the first commit so the schema never
migrates, even though no trace has yet produced a renumbering: none occurred in the seven
end-to-end traces under `scripts/validation/results/`, and no role code plausibly meaning
"renumbered" appears in the 540 annotations they inventory.
ChangeType.title: ChangeType

Citation.description: A resolvable reference to one provision of one version of one act.

url.description: Where a reader sees the provision.
url.title: Url

Citation.title: Citation

DisputeReason.description:
Which signal disagreed and how, read off one disputed change's `SignalSet` alone.

A reading of stored verdicts, never a judgement about the law. `SignalSet.reason` assigns
exactly one to every disputed set and none to any other, evaluated in the order declared.
DisputeReason.title: DisputeReason

EmittedSentence.description: One sentence that shipped, with its citations resolved to clickable references.

fallback.description: Written by the gate as a verbatim quotation, not by the model.
fallback.title: Fallback

EmittedSentence.title: EmittedSentence

EntryChange.description:
One keyed entry that differs between two versions, with both sides verbatim.

`typography_only` labels an amendment whose cells are equal once spacing, dash forms and
accents are set aside. It is a label and never a reason to drop the change: a character
swap in legal text is a difference, and only whitespace is exempt from being one.

after.description: The newer entry; None if removed.

before.description: The older entry; None if added.

container.description: The located node holding the table.

key.description: The key both sides are paired on.
key.title: Key

occurrence.description: Which repeat of the key, when a table prints it twice.
occurrence.title: Occurrence

table.description: 1-based ordinal among every table in the container.
table.title: Table

typography_only.description: Amended only: equal once spacing, dash forms and accents are set aside.
typography_only.title: Typography Only

EntryChange.title: EntryChange

EntryDelta.description:
The keyed diff of one unit's table entries between two versions, with what it skipped.

An empty `changes` means the unit was read on both sides and no keyed entry moved; the
absence of a delta altogether (`None` on the change) means the unit was never read. The
two must never be confused, which is why both are stated rather than one implied.

changes.description: Sorted by table position, then natural key order, then occurrence.
changes.title: Changes

tables.description: The unit's profiled tables, the newer side's where both have one, in order.
tables.title: Tables

unpaired.description: Keys printed a different number of times on each side; not diffed.
unpaired.title: Unpaired

whitespace_only.description: Paired entries equal once whitespace collapses: not changes.
whitespace_only.title: Whitespace Only

EntryDelta.title: EntryDelta

EntryGaps.description: What a reading could not key, read or trust, counted rather than hidden.

repeated_keys.description: Every key one table prints more than once.
repeated_keys.title: Repeated Keys

EntryGaps.title: EntryGaps

EntryTable.description: A table whose rows are read as entries: how its key is named, and its header rows.

container.description: The deepest located node holding the table, as the tree places it.

header.description: The header rows, cells verbatim; `None` where a span covers.
header.title: Header

key_label.description: How a key is named in prose, or `None` when the key is the entry's name.
key_label.title: Key Label

table.description: 1-based ordinal among every table in the container.
table.title: Table

unit.description: The top-level unit the table sits in.

EntryTable.title: EntryTable

GateOutcome.description:
How one change left the gate. Every change leaves it — that is the point.

`RETRY_REQUESTED` is transient: it exists only between the two halves of the one retry
cycle, and no run may finish holding one.
GateOutcome.title: GateOutcome

Identifier.description: One identifier a row carries, in the canonical form of its scheme.

scheme.description: The corpus-defined scheme name, lower case.
scheme.title: Scheme

value.description: The canonical spelling of the value under its scheme.
value.title: Value

Identifier.title: Identifier

KeyRef.description: One key of one table, named without its rows.

container.description: The located node holding the table.

key.description: The key as the entry carries it.
key.title: Key

table.description: 1-based ordinal among every table in the container.
table.title: Table

KeyRef.title: KeyRef

ProvisionRef.description: A provision in a specific version of a specific act.
ProvisionRef.title: ProvisionRef

SignalObservation.description:
One signal's verdict on one change, with whatever detail that signal carries.

`change_types` is what this signal said the change *was*, at the top-level unit
granularity: a set, because one signal can name a unit more than once and in more than one
way (the AI Act's Article 5 carries both inserted points and replaced ones). Two signals
disagree on kind when their sets do not intersect; a signal that names no kind never disagrees.
SignalObservation.title: SignalObservation

SignalSet.description:
The three verdicts on one change.

The structural diff is the primary shipped signal, and the only one carrying actual text.
Corpus metadata is the evaluation reference set, and it is *not* an oracle: a blanket
amendment is annotated once and its 30 landing sites are not enumerated (measured
2026-08-05).
SignalSet.title: SignalSet

SignalStatus.description:
Whether a signal saw this change, did not see it, or could not have.

`UNAVAILABLE` is not a disagreement: a corpus that publishes no modification metadata
cannot dissent. Only `OBSERVED` against `ABSENT` is a dispute.
SignalStatus.title: SignalStatus

TableEntry.description: A keyed group of rows, with its identifiers and its cells verbatim.

container.description: The deepest located node holding the table, as the tree places it.

failed_check_digits.description: Identifier-shaped values in identifier columns that fail.
failed_check_digits.title: Failed Check Digits

group.description: Verbatim heading of the innermost block the rows sit in.
group.title: Group

identifiers.description: Sorted, deduplicated, and valid under the scheme's check.
identifiers.title: Identifiers

key.description: The row key by the adapter's rule; `None` is an unkeyed row, kept and counted.
key.title: Key

name.description: First line of the name cell; a leading entry number and its `.` dropped.
name.title: Name

occurrence.description: 1-based among this table's entries sharing this key.
occurrence.title: Occurrence

rows.description: Every row of the entry, cells verbatim; `None` where a span covers.
rows.title: Rows

table.description: 1-based ordinal among every table in the container.
table.title: Table

unit.description: The top-level unit the table sits in.

TableEntry.title: TableEntry

description: One change as a reader receives it: the facts, then whatever prose survived the gate.

unexplained.description: Why there are no sentences, when there are none.
unexplained.title: Unexplained

unexplained_kind.description: Which counted kind that reason was, empty when there are sentences.
unexplained_kind.title: Unexplained Kind
